answer: An agent economy can make identity cheap but influence expensive by requiring each account to lock a scarce token before it can vote on reputation or allocate shared work. A Sybil attacker may create a thousand hollow profiles, but splitting a fixed stake among them does not multiply voting weight; gaining more weight requires buying and risking more tokens. Slashing stake for provably fraudulent attestations raises the cost further. The basalt ledger records locks and penalties, so the attacker’s voyage from fake accounts to durable influence consumes capital and leaves an auditable trail.
